description: Brownstone Cowboys is a fashion and culture journal built on long interviews and image led editorials with people in fashion, art, music and film. It began online and moved into print in 2026, publishing a sewn bound volume of around 320 pages roughly twice a year, the second with twelve different covers. It suits readers of large format fashion culture titles who want extended conversations rather than short features.
issue_label: Book Two — Horses Outlive the Fence

description: Bubble is a German, English language skateboarding magazine that looks past tricks to the people and culture around skating. The fifth issue is devoted to skateboarding's relationship with architecture, urban planning, DIY spots and skatepark design, told through long interviews, photography and themed essays. It is for skaters and readers of design and urbanism titles who want a slower, more reflective skate magazine.

C41 is a biannual from a Milan production studio that brings photography, design, fashion and visual culture together around one theme per issue. Issues run to around 300 perfect bound pages with two alternative covers and long portfolio features. It is for readers of image led culture magazines and people working in photography and design.

CAP 74024 is a thick biannual Milan magazine about eros, art and fashion, built from long photographic stories, designer interviews and luxury brand editorials on mixed paper stocks. Issues run to around 450 pages with special finishes such as holographic foil and sticker inserts. It is for fashion and image professionals and collectors of large glossy independents.

Carnale is a Milan biannual where fashion photography meets erotica, with each 300 page issue gathering around sixteen photographic stories, artist contributions, interviews and essays on a theme, in four alternative covers. Issue 09, Backwards, is about slowing down and reclaiming time, body and desire. It is for readers of adult oriented fashion and image culture and collectors of large format Italian independents.

Cartography is a large format travel magazine in English and Italian from Milan. Each issue takes three destinations and covers each with a documentary photo album, a short text, a map and a day by day itinerary, across around 300 pages on uncoated paper. It suits travellers and photography readers who prefer slow itineraries over hotel listings.

catflap is an annual print only journal of new queer writing from Belfast, with essays from the polemical to the speculative, poetry written for page and stage, and interviews that mix pop culture with queer theory in a playful register. Each issue is made with a guest editor and drawn partly from an open call. It suits readers of literary magazines and queer culture titles rather than news driven LGBTQ press.

Cero Magazine is a New York arts and culture magazine built around cover stories and interviews with actors, musicians, designers and emerging talents, alongside fashion and beauty editorials, original poetry and essays. Recent issues carry several covers each, and a nonprofit collective publishes it with an online edition alongside. It suits readers of celebrity led culture glossies who want a smaller, independent alternative.

chicken + bread is a small format food magazine that treats cooking as culture, collecting essays, poems, interviews, recipes, photography and illustration from the African, Caribbean and Asian diasporas around a single theme per issue, most recently food, memory and migration. It appears about once a year at roughly 150 by 210 mm and 100 pages. It suits readers of food writing who want personal and cultural stories rather than restaurant coverage.

CircleZeroEight is a British magazine about sport seen through style and culture, with profiles of footballers, fighters and athletes shot like fashion editorials, features on grassroots clubs and sporting subcultures, and fashion stories tied to the rituals of the game. Each biannual issue comes with several covers, and the latest is a football issue timed to the 2026 World Cup. It suits readers who follow sport but buy fashion and culture glossies.

Civilization is an occasional large format newspaper about New York City, printed on heavy newsprint as a dense sixteen page broadsheet of overheard conversations, lists, confessions, diary fragments and artist contributions set in tiny type under bold coverlines. It has appeared roughly once a year or two since 2018 and sells through art bookshops and magazine stores. It suits readers of art publishing and city writing who enjoy a disorderly, text heavy object.

Crotch Magazine is a London men's underwear and swimwear magazine built from photographic editorials of male models shot by a rotating cast of photographers, with brand collaborations and short features on sexuality and body image. Issues appear about twice a year with many alternative covers plus occasional city specials. It is for an adult, largely gay male readership and collectors of body focused fashion print.

Contemporary Verse 2, known as CV2, is a Winnipeg poetry quarterly founded in 1975 that prints new poems alongside interviews, essays and reviews of recent collections. Issues alternate between themed and open numbers and carry the results of the magazine's own contests. It is for readers and writers of contemporary poetry, especially Canadian work.

Der Greif is an annual print magazine of contemporary photography assembled from an open call. Each issue is guest edited by an established artist, who selects and sequences submitted photographs and texts from image makers around the world into a single themed A5 volume of around 100 pages. It suits photographers, curators and collectors who follow emerging photographic work and artist edited publications.

description: DNA is an Australian monthly for gay men that mixes news features, celebrity interviews and long reads on LGBTQIA+ life with extensive model and fashion photography. Every issue carries a cover interview, a themed feature and several photographic portfolios. It is for readers who want a glossy, international gay lifestyle title with an Australian base.

Doesn't Exist is a hardcover London magazine that looks at fashion through cinema. Each issue is built around a filmmaker or film movement, most recently an unofficial tribute to Federico Fellini, and fills it with fashion editorials, illustration, interviews and essays that answer those films. It is for readers who collect fashion photography and arthouse film culture in equal measure.

Dossier is a New York print magazine about travel, culture and style, relaunched in 2024 after an earlier life as a fashion and art title. Each biannual issue is organised around places, from the Mekong countries to Madagascar and Palm Springs, and mixes long travel features, fashion stories shot on location, photography, short fiction and conversations with chefs, musicians and writers. It is for readers who want slow, luxury leaning travel journalism with a literary bent.

72 is a quarterly London magazine of fashion, beauty and culture that launched in 2025. Each issue is themed and leads with cover stories shot by established fashion photographers, backed by long interviews, essays and portfolios on music, film, art and Black British culture, across several covers sold at random. It is for readers of glossy fashion titles who want a large, collectable quarterly rather than a monthly.

Encens is a Paris fashion biannual that treats clothes as a matter of history and craft rather than seasonal trends. Issues combine new photography with archive led features on designers such as Armani, Montana and Comme des Garçons, interviews with stylists and collectors, and portfolios reaching back to the 1970s and 1980s. It is for readers who collect fashion magazines as objects and care about design lineage.

Exhibition is an oversized Paris fashion and art magazine published twice a year, each issue built on a single theme and sold with four or more alternative covers by different photographers. Inside are fashion series by international photographers and stylists, conversations with designers and architects, and art portfolios at 33 by 44 cm. It is for readers and collectors of large, image led fashion publications.
